samples.summary: fitPattern produces NaN dash values for a non-finite scaled pattern, silently rendering a dashed border as solid
samples.evidence: `fitPattern` computes `cycle = pattern.reduce(...)` and returns `pattern.map(n => (n * max) / cycle)`. `width` reaches `StrokePreview` from `value?.width` (border-picker.tsx:208), i.e. a persisted stroke width the content API lets a caller set to any number. For a width around 1e308, `dashArray` returns `[6*w, 4*w]` = `[Infinity, Infinity]`, `cycle` is `Infinity`, and `Infinity * 32 / Infinity` is `NaN`, so `strokeDasharray` becomes `"NaN NaN"` — an invalid SVG attribute the browser drops, making every dash row preview as a solid line. `dashArray` itself deliberately guards its own degenerate-width case (render-context.ts:94-99) but the new scaling reintroduces one.

samples.summary: Table cell borders carry a `dash` that the canvas renders but the PPTX exporter never writes, so it is lost on export
samples.evidence: `CellBorder` has `dash?: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted'` (model/element.ts:435) and `table-renderer.ts:314` strokes it via `dashArray(edge.stroke.dash, ...)`, but `export/pptx/table.ts:120` emits `<a:ln${side} w="${w}">${solidFillXml(color)}</a:ln${side}>` with no `<a:prstDash>`, and `import/pptx/table.ts:207-224` (`parseCellBorder`) never reads one. Now that `dashXml` is a shared helper exported from `connector.ts` and used by both other `<a:ln>` emitters, the table path is the one remaining stroke emitter that drops dash: a dashed cell border round-trips as solid. Reach is limited because no frontend control sets a cell dash today (grepped the frontend for table+dash), so it is only reachable through the content API.

samples.summary: fitPattern doc comment states the wrong untouched-weight range
samples.evidence: The comment says "Patterns that already repeat (every weight up to 3px) are returned untouched." The threshold is `cycle <= 32`: dashed cycle is `10*w`, so untouched up to w = 3 (3.2), but dotted cycle is `4*w`, untouched all the way to w = 8. The stated range is wrong for `'dotted'`, which is half the patterns this function handles.

finding.summary: Removing the preview weight clamp makes "Dashed" render as a fully solid line at the largest border weight
finding.evidence: `StrokePreview` now draws into a fixed 64px-wide box (`PREVIEW_W = 64`) with `pattern = dashArray(dash, width)`. At width 16, `dashArray('dashed', 16)` = `[96, 64]` — the first dash alone (96px) is longer than the entire 64px preview line, so the Dashed row in the dash menu (border-picker.tsx:208, fed `value?.width`) and the 16px row in the weight menu (border-picker.tsx:175) paint an unbroken line, indistinguishable from Solid. Dotted at 16 gives `[32,32]`, i.e. one dash and one gap. The canvas is fine because shapes are far wider than 64px, but the picker — whose whole job is to distinguish the three dash styles — now shows the same drawing for two different choices. The deleted `DASH_PREVIEW_MAX_WEIGHT` was what prevented this; nothing replaced it (e.g. scaling the pattern to the preview length).

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is not present in the repository. It claims `StrokePreview` computes `pattern = dashArray(dash, width)` with no replacement for the deleted `DASH_PREVIEW_MAX_WEIGHT` clamp. In fact stroke-preview.tsx:61 reads `const pattern = fitPattern(dashArray(dash, width));`, and stroke-preview.tsx:26-31 defines `fitPattern`, which is exactly the "scaling the pattern to the preview length" mitigation the finding says is missing: it sums the cycle and, when the cycle exceeds `PREVIEW_W / 2` (32), scales every element by `max / cycle` so two whole cycles fit in the 64px box. Running the finding's own numbers against `dashArray` (render-context.ts:99-102): dashed@16 = [96,64], cycle 160 > 32, scaled to [19.2,12.8] — two full on/off cycles inside the line, so it renders with visible gaps, not as a solid line; dotted@16 = [32,32] scales to [16,16], preserving the 1.5:1 vs 1:1 ratio that distinguishes Dashed from Dotted. Solid yields [] (cycle 0, returned untouched) and line 86 omits the attribute. Both cited call sites (border-picker.tsx:175 weight menu and border-picker.tsx:208 dash menu) go through the same single `StrokePreview` component — grep shows it is the only definition and there are only these two usages — so no path reaches the raw pattern. The surviving `DASH_PREVIEW_MAX_WEIGHT` matches are a prose comment (render-context.ts:78) and task docs, not live code. The described defect therefore does not exist as stated.

finding.summary: Connector dash is now imported but still never exported, so a dashed connector loses its dash on PPTX export
finding.evidence: `parseCxnSp` resolves its stroke through `parseShapeStroke` (import/pptx/shape.ts:1054), which this change taught to read `<a:prstDash>` — so an imported connector now carries `dash`. The connector exporter builds its own line element without any `prstDash`: `const ln = `<a:ln w="${lnW}">${fillXml}${headXml}${tailXml}</a:ln>`` (export/pptx/connector.ts:110); it does not go through `lineXml`, which is the only place `DASH_VAL`/`<a:prstDash>` is emitted (export/pptx/shape.ts:153). Result: import a deck with a dashed connector (or set a dash on a connector in the toolbar), export, and the dash is silently dropped — the exact asymmetry the new shape round-trip test closes for shapes only. The new round-trip case (test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts:241) covers shapes, not connectors, so nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: The claim that the connector exporter never emits the dash is false. connector.ts defines its OWN DASH_VAL map and exported dashXml() helper at lines 92-101; the doc comment states it lives there, rather than beside lineXml in shape.ts, precisely because both exporters need it and the reverse direction would close an import cycle. Grep confirms 'prstDash' has ZERO occurrences in src/export/pptx/shape.ts, so the premise that lineXml is 'the only place DASH_VAL/prstDash is emitted' is backwards. The actual line-building code at connector.ts:137,140 reads: const dash = dashXml(stroke?.dash); then const ln = a:ln w=lnW followed by fillXml + dash + headXml + tailXml. The dash IS interpolated, between the fill and the arrowheads per CT_LineProperties ordering, with optional chaining guarding the no-stroke path. The evidence string quoted in the finding (an a:ln without the dash slot, attributed to line 110) does not exist in the file: line 110 is a doc comment, and line 114 documents stroke.dash to a:prstDash val as part of the declared round-trip contract. Four dedicated tests at test/export/pptx/connector.test.ts:73-120 assert dashed to dash, dotted to sysDot, solid/absent/no-stroke emit nothing, and correct ordering relative to the closing solidFill and the tailEnd. The reviewer's searches were scoped to src/export for prstDash|lineXml and to round-trip.test.ts, which missed connector.ts and connector.test.ts. The round-trip test not covering connectors is a test-coverage observation, moot given the unit tests and outside the Correctness lane regardless.
